headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that Virginia's primary electric provider propose rates to the SCC that allocate costs for increasing electric generating capacity to large energy users (25 MW or more), preventing these costs from being passed to other customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Pass Legislation Shifting Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: Virginia's legislature passed HB 1393, which requires the State Corporation Commission to establish rates that shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity to high-demand users, specifically data centers consuming 25 MW or more. This measure aims to prevent these infrastructure costs from being passed on to other customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency and data for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Shelly Simonds.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/potential for future regulation).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Data Center Water Use
news_summary: Virginia's General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report monthly or quarterly water volumes provided to data centers, including reclaimed water. This legislation aims to provide better data for state and local planners to understand the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources, especially given concerns about dwindling groundwater.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for noise impacts on residential units and schools within 500 feet of new high energy use facilities (data centers) and allows for assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, parks, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental and conservation groups, historic preservation advocates.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations.
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Siting and Noise Studies
news_summary: HB 153, signed into law, mandates that Virginia localities require site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools before approving new data centers consuming 100 MW or more. The law also allows localities to request impact reviews on water, farmland, parks, and historic sites, providing more local control over data center development.
